unit: WF4 Distil Sources registry provenance, content alignment and heading-anchored excerpting
description: Negative control: with pairedItem stripped from every response, every row fails closed as SOURCE_PROVENANCE_UNKNOWN and no url is stored.
why_it_exists: Execution 329 (a real matter): every Sources row was written with the WRONG URL against its own title and excerpt, pairwise swapped. The url was resolved as `j.url || (ctx.urls || [])[i]`; Fetch Source runs with fullResponse: true and returns only data, headers, statusCode and statusMessage, so there is never a j.url and the positional fallback always won - and ctx.urls is a legacy list built by Build Draft Context in a DIFFERENT order from the Source Registry that actually drove the fetches. The result was a citation whose link points at a different Act: fabricated authority wearing a correct-looking title. The fallback was deleted and replaced by two independent controls, n8n pairedItem provenance and a declared-phrase content check. The whole point of the fix is that it never guesses by array index. This case removes the only provable link back to a registry entry and asserts the code refuses rather than falling back to position.
